source_text:
Γέγραπται γὰρ οὕτως: Καὶ ἐγένετο μεθ̓ ἡμέρας, ἤνεγκεν Κάϊν ἀπὸ τῶν καρπῶν τῆς γῆς θυσίαν τῷ θεῷ, καὶ Ἄβελ ἤνεγκεν καὶ αὐτὸς ἀπὸ τῶν πρωτοτόκων τῶν προβάτων καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν στεάτων αὐτῶν.
καὶ ἐπεῖδεν ὁ θεὸς ἐπὶ Ἄβελ καὶ ἐπὶ τοῖς δώροις αὐτοῦ, ἐπὶ δὲ Κάϊν καὶ ἐπὶ ταῖς θυσίαις αὐτοῦ οὐ προσέσχεν.
καὶ ἐλυπήθη Κάϊν λίαν καὶ συνέπεσεν τῷ προσώπῳ αὐτοῦ.
καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς πρὸς Κάϊν: Ἱνατί περίλυπος ἐγένου, καὶ ἱνατί συνέπεσεν τὸ πρόσωπόν σου; οὐκ ἐὰν ὀρθῶς προσενέγκῃς, ὀρθῶς δὲ μὴ διέλῃς, ἥμαρτες;
ἡσύχασον: πρὸς σὲ ή ἀποστροφὴ αὐτοῦ, καὶ σὺ ἄρξεις αὐτοῦ.
καὶ εἶπεν Κάϊν πρὸς Ἄβελ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ: Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πεδίον. καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ, ἀνέστη Κάϊν ἐπὶ Ἄβελ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπέκτεινεν αὐτόν.
ὁρᾶτε, ἀδελφοί, ζῆλος καὶ φθόνος ἀδελφοκτονίαν κατειργάσατο.
διὰ ζῆλος ὁ πατὴρ ἡμῶν Ἰακὼβ ἀπέδρα ἀπὸ προσώπου Ἠσαῦ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ.
ζῆλος ἐποίησεν Ἰωσὴφ μέχρι θανάτου διωχθῆναι καὶ μέχρι δουλείας εἰσελθεῖν.
ζῆλος φυγεῖν ἠνάγκασεν Μωϋσῆν ἀπὸ προσώπου Φαραὼ βασιλέως Αἰγύπτου ἐν τῷ ἀκοῦσαι αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τοῦ ὁμοφύλου: Τίς σε κατέστησεν κριτὴν ἢ δικαστὴν ἐφ̓ ἡμῶν; μὴ ἀνελεῖν με σὺ θέλεις, ὃν τρόπον ἀνεῖλες ἐχθὲς τὸν Λἰγύπτιον;
διὰ ζῆλος ʼΛαρὼν καὶ Μαριὰμ ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς ηὐλίσθησαν.
ζῆλος Δαθὰν καὶ Ἀβειρὼν ζῶντας κατήγαγεν εἰς ᾅδου διὰ τὸ στασιάσαι αὐτοὺς πρὸς τὸν θεράποντα τοῦ θεοῦ Μωϋσῆν.
διὰ ζῆλος Δαυεὶδ φθόνον ἔσχεν οὐ μόνον ὑπὸ τῶν ἀλλοφύλων, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑπὸ Σαοὺλ βασιλέως Ἰσραὴλ ἐδιώχθη.
orientation: The Roman church has just begun its letter to Corinth and now opens its scriptural argument by showing how envy has worked murder and persecution from the very first brothers onward.
pass_a_gloss: For it has been written thus: And it came to pass after days, Cain brought from the fruits of the earth a sacrifice to God, and Abel brought also himself from the firstborn of the sheep and from their fats. And God looked upon Abel and upon his gifts, but upon Cain and upon his sacrifices he did not attend. And Cain was grieved exceedingly and his face fell. And God said to Cain: Why have you become deeply grieved, and why has your face fallen? Not if you offer rightly, but if you do not divide rightly, have you sinned? Be still: to you [shall be] his turning, and you shall rule over him. And Cain said to Abel his brother: Let us go through into the plain. And it came to pass in their being in the plain, Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him. You see, brothers, envy and spite worked brother-murder. Through envy our father Jacob fled from the face of Esau his brother. Envy made Joseph be pursued as far as death and to enter as far as slavery. Envy forced Moses to flee from the face of Pharaoh king of Egypt when he heard from the fellow-tribesman: Who appointed you judge or magistrate over us? Do you wish to kill me, in the way you killed yesterday the Egyptian? Through envy Aaron and Mariam lodged outside the camp. Envy brought Dathan and Abiram down alive into Hades because of their making faction against the servant of God Moses. Through envy David had spite not only from the foreigners, but also was persecuted by Saul king of Israel.

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for the root cause of the Corinthian strife; kept consistent throughout the section.
Distinct from ζῆλος; renders the active ill-will that accompanies envy, avoiding the banned 'jealousy'.
Literal compound rendering that preserves the force of the Greek word for killing a brother.
Uses the fixed glossary noun 'faction' to render the cognate verb, tying Dathan and Abiram's sin to the Corinthian στάσις.
Renders the verb of favorable regard; 'attend' keeps the sense of God turning his attention toward an offering.
Preserves the intensity of λίαν and the emotional force of λυπέω.

pass_b_english: For it is written this way: “After some days had passed, Cain brought a sacrifice to God from the fruits of the earth, and Abel also brought one from the firstborn of his sheep and from their fat portions.
God looked with favor on Abel and his gifts, but on Cain and his sacrifices He did not attend.
Cain was grieved exceedingly, and his face fell.
God said to Cain, ‘Why are you so deeply grieved, and why has your face fallen? If you offer rightly but do not divide rightly, have you not sinned?
Be still. His turning is toward you, and you will rule over him.’
Cain said to his brother Abel, ‘Let us go out into the plain.’ And while they were in the plain, Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.”
You see, brothers, envy and spite brought about brother-murder.
Because of envy, our father Jacob fled from the face of his brother Esau.
Envy caused Joseph to be pursued to the point of death and to enter into slavery.

Envy forced Moses to flee from the face of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, when he heard his fellow-tribesman say, “Who appointed you judge or magistrate over us? Do you want to kill me, just as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?”
Because of envy, Aaron and Miriam had to lodge outside the camp.
Envy brought Dathan and Abiram down alive into Hades, because they made faction against Moses, the servant of God.
Because of envy, David incurred envy not only from the foreigners, but he was also pursued by Saul, king of Israel.

problems.why: φθόνον ἔσχεν is 'had envy' or 'was envied' or 'experienced envy', not 'suffered spite'. While 'suffered spite' captures some sense, it's interpretive. More importantly, the structure 'David suffered spite not only from the foreigners' makes 'spite' the object of suffering, but φθόνον is what David had directed at him - 'David had envy [directed at him]'. The English makes it sound like David suffered from spite, but the Greek says he had envy from others. The agency is slightly off.
problems.fix: David was envied not only by foreigners

problems.why: φθόνον ἔσχεν means 'experienced envy/jealousy directed at him,' not 'suffered spite.'
problems.ruling: φθόνον ἔσχεν means 'had envy directed at him,' not 'suffered spite'; 'spite' misrepresents the Greek and breaks the pattern of 'envy' as subject throughout.

fixed: The English 'suffered spite' was interpretive and misrepresented the agency of φθόνον ἔσχεν; changed to 'was envied' to reflect that envy was directed at David.

problems.ruling: ηὐλίσθησαν is simple aorist 'lodged'; 'had to' adds compulsion absent from the Greek verb.

problems.ruling: ἀποστροφὴ αὐτοῦ refers to sin's turning (Gen 4:7 context), not 'His'; capital H misleads reader on subject.

last_rejected.quote: If you offer rightly but do not divide rightly, have you not sinned?
last_rejected.source_quote: οὐκ ἐὰν ὀρθῶς προσενέγκῃς, ὀρθῶς δὲ μὴ διέλῃς, ἥμαρτες;
last_rejected.why: Greek asks a rhetorical question expecting 'yes' (you have sinned); English 'have you not sinned?' flips to expecting 'no'.
last_rejected.fix: If you offer rightly but do not divide rightly, have you sinned? Be still.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek οὐκ...ἥμαρτες; is a rhetorical question expecting 'yes'; English 'have you not sinned?' conveys same meaning correctly.

last_rejected.quote: Its desire is toward you, and you will rule over it.
last_rejected.source_quote: πρὸς σὲ ἡ ἀποστροφὴ αὐτοῦ, καὶ σὺ ἄρξεις αὐτοῦ.
last_rejected.why: Greek says 'his/its turning/returning is toward you' (sin's desire/crouching), but 'desire' misreads ἀποστροφή; standard LXX rendering is 'turning'.
last_rejected.fix: Its turning is toward you, and you shall rule over it.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀποστροφή can mean 'turning'; 'desire' follows Gen 4:7 tradition. Defensible rendering, not a major error.

last_rejected.quote: Because of envy, David incurred envy not only from the foreigners
last_rejected.source_quote: διὰ ζῆλος Δαυεὶδ φθόνον ἔσχεν οὐ μόνον ὑπὸ τῶν ἀλλοφύλων
last_rejected.why: Greek says David 'had envy/spite' (φθόνον ἔσχεν) from others; English 'incurred envy' makes David the object of envy, but 'had envy' means he experienced/was subject to hostile envy.
last_rejected.fix: Because of envy, David suffered envy not only from the foreigners
last_rejected.ruling: φθόνον ἔσχεν with ὑπὸ τῶν ἀλλοφύλων naturally means David received envy from others; 'incurred envy' is accurate.
